question: Should typed transient tool-progress payloads in Slack default to reaction-or-suppression instead of being posted as normal chat messages when no standalone-progress setting opts them in?
rationale: This is an intentional user-visible delivery-policy change; tests establish the proposed mechanics but cannot determine the durable Slack product default or the acceptable fail-closed behavior when no reaction target exists.

options.title: Confirm reaction-or-suppression policy
options.body: Accept the private Slack policy after current-head agent-path proof shows marked progress is hidden while ordinary and explicitly enabled standalone progress remain deliverable.

options.title: Preserve posting by default
options.body: Require an explicit opt-in or revised policy if existing Slack progress posts must remain visible for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Confirm reaction-or-suppression policy
recommendation.body: Accept the private Slack policy after current-head agent-path proof shows marked progress is hidden while ordinary and explicitly enabled standalone progress remain deliverable.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the direct implementation context and can supply the requested current-head proof, while a repository Slack-area owner should make the final product decision.
